subject: Business Models
title: Apple: Computers to Ecosystem
description: A 60-second lesson on Apple: Computers to Ecosystem.

hook.text: In 2001, Apple was a computer company in decline. Steve Jobs bet on a music player. Everything changed.

buildup.text: The iPod was a product. iTunes was a store. Together they were a platform controlling how people bought music.

discovery.text: Apple learned that hardware + software + services creates lock-in. One product leads to the next purchase.

twist.text: Apple's services revenue (App Store, iCloud, Music) now exceeds $85 billion/year—larger than most tech companies.

climax.text: Apple pivoted from selling computers to selling an ecosystem. The model, not hardware, built the $3T company.

punchline.text: iPod to iPhone to services. Apple's model pivot built a $3T company.

quiz.question: What does Apple's ecosystem model create for customers?
options: Lock-in through hardware + software + services integration
